text:
anna_sales: FYI — NovaHealth deal: they expect 99th pct < 500ms for chat and have committed to 3 reserved A100 GPUs. Need a concise onboarding runbook, answers to the security questionnaire, and a cost estimate by EOD. Who can own sizing, preheat, and pricing?

 taylor_solutions: I can own the runbook and presales checklist. Can someone paste the expected traffic shape (RPS) and average prompt/response sizes?

 anna_sales: Quick numbers: peak ~120 qps sustained for chat, average prompt ~220 tokens, average response ~160 tokens. Daily burst window: up to 220 qps for ~10 minutes once/day. SLA asks: 99.9% availability, 99th latency target 500ms. Data residency: US-only. HIPAA flagged — legal will send questionnaire.

 devon_sre: Notes on sizing: with KV prefix caching + batching, 120 sustained qps maps to ~2 A100s for our gptx-8b-ish family. 3 reserved gives redundancy + headroom. Suggest autoscale policy: min_reserved=3, max=6 (burst), scale_step=1 GPU, cooldown=180s. Preheat process: run KV warmers and a short synthetic traffic sweep on new nodes before routing production. Plan a quantized-model fallback for cost/availability events.

 liam_eng: Quantization guidance: recommend testing NF4 (4-bit) for the model to reduce latency/cost; if quality regresses, fallback to int8 or fp16. Quick runtime snippet to include in runbook:

 ```yaml
 model_variant: "gptx-2-8b"
 quantization_profile: "nf4-medium"
 batching:
   max_batch_tokens: 2048
   max_concurrent_requests: 48
 routing:
   fallback_on_load: true
 ```

 I'll run evals on the customer prompt set tonight.

 security_bot: Security checklist items to attach: KMS integration required, key rotation policy, audit log retention (1y), VPC peering, TLS in transit + at-rest encryption, SOC2 report, and HIPAA BAA. Also ask: any third-party PHI sinks? If yes, need Data Flow diagram.

 taylor_solutions: Runbook outline I'll draft: 1) Traffic profile + sizing rationale, 2) Preheat steps + warm scripts, 3) Autoscale policy & stepdown rules, 4) Monitoring + alerting thresholds + ticketing playbook, 5) Fallback routing & model variants, 6) Billing impact summary. Draft ETA ~90m.

 anna_sales: Devon / Liam — please list the top 4 failure modes we should document (very short bullets).

 devon_sre: Failure modes: 1) Spot eviction -> failover to reserved pool & AZ failover; 2) Model-load OOM on node -> kill oldest idle session, restart process; 3) Long-tail token storms -> per-tenant rate limits, circuit breaker; 4) KV cache coldstart -> preheat + synthetic warmers. Runbook command example:

 ```bash
 # preheat warmers
 for f in prompts/*.json; do curl -X POST https://api.redwood.run/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -d "@$f"; done
 ```

 liam_eng: Short billing note for legal: Reserved GPUs are billed at the committed (flat) rate; any autoscaled GPUs beyond the reservation are billed on-demand/spot and appear on top of the commit. We can offer a capped burst-credit pool to bound customer spend during autoscale events.

 anna_sales: Perfect. Legal wants a one-paragraph explanation of autoscale impact on the commit — I'll forward Liam's sentence. Also they asked for the security checklist — security_bot can you attach template?

 security_bot: Attached questionnaire template (link internal) and a checklist PDF. Will also add an audit log sample and recommended retention policy.

 taylor_solutions: Draft posted internally: https://redwood/internal/runbooks/novahealth-6280012345 — please review for wording and run commands.

 devon_sre: Reviewed draft, left two comments around cooldown and AZ spread. Recommend cooldown 180-240s and spread reserved GPUs across 2 AZs if possible.

 liam_eng: I'll run perf smoke tests against the sample prompts tonight and post 50/90/99 latencies + throughput numbers in the doc.

 anna_sales: Great — closing loop: ETA EOD for runbook + cost calc + security answers. Thanks team! :thumbsup:
